title: Compute initial prestress
action: For each given biaxial prestretch λ (1.15 and 1.38), compute the first strain invariant I1 = 2λ^2 + 1/λ^4, then the initial in-plane stress σ0 = 2(λ^2 - 1/λ^4)[C10 + 2C20(I1-3) + 3C30(I1-3)^2] using the provided Yeoh constants.
description: Compute initial hyperelastic prestress from prestretch, which drives all subsequent steps.

title: Static center displacement at 80 dB
action: Using the computed prestress and membrane geometry, calculate the static center deflection for each prestretch at a uniform pressure corresponding to 80 dB SPL (re 20 µPa). Use the modal solution for a pinned square membrane and truncate the double series over odd m,n until convergence. Write the center displacement in nanometers.
description: Static center displacement for prestretch values 1.15 and 1.38 at 80 dB incident SPL.

title: Normalized mode shape along centerline
action: For the prestretch λ=1.38, compute the static displacement profile along the centerline y/b = 0.5 for normalized x-coordinate from 0 to 1. Evaluate the same modal series, normalize by the maximum displacement, and write the normalized (x, displacement) pairs.
description: Normalized displacement along the centerline for λ=1.38, used to validate the mode shape prediction.

title: Fundamental resonance frequencies
action: For each prestretch, compute the lumped acoustic parameters: membrane mass M_aM = 1.3785 ρ h / b^2, compliance C_aM = 0.0351 b^4 / (σ h), radiation mass M_aRad = 1.486 ⋅ b ρ / (2 b^2) (including recess effect). For the case with electrodes, add the electrode acoustic mass M_aE calculated from the given electrode density (1010 kg/m³) and thickness (25 µm) using the same lumped mass expression. Then compute the fundamental resonance frequency f = 1/(2π sqrt((M_aM+M_aRad+M_aE) ⋅ C_aM)). Output a row with prestretch, a boolean for electrodes, and the frequency in Hz.
description: Fundamental resonance frequencies for both prestretches, with and without electrodes, compared to experimental values.

title: Normalized resonance frequency vs voltage
action: For each prestretch, compute the effective permittivity εr = -0.28 λ + 2.76. For voltages from 0 to 5 kV in steps of 0.5 kV, compute the reduced stress σ(V) = σ0 – ε0 εr (λ^2 V / h0)^2, the corresponding compliance C_aM(V), and then the resonance frequency f(V) using the total mass with electrodes included. Normalize by f(0) and write the normalized frequency.
description: Normalized resonance frequency f(V)/f(0) for 0–5 kV, validating the voltage tuning effect.
